reasoning:
Recent data for Rhode Island’s 2026 U.S. Senate race show incumbent Democrat Jack Reed with extremely large leads in both primary and general-election polling, and there is no recent, state-specific presidential general-election polling in the last 45 days.
An Embold Research poll for Salve Regina University’s Pell Center conducted August 3–11 finds Reed at 61% to Democratic primary challenger Connor Burbridge’s 12%, a Reed +49 margin among Democratic primary voters, consistent with earlier UNH polling showing Reed leads of +28 to +50 in primary and hypothetical general matchups; these margins, combined with the state’s D+8 Cook PVI, indicate a structurally safe Democratic Senate seat.[1][2][12][5]
Because no recent general-election presidential polling for Rhode Island appears in the last 45 days, the best available structural indicator for statewide partisan lean is Cook’s statewide PVI of D+8, which supports treating the current environment as strongly Democratic-leaning overall, but with quantified margins only for the Senate race rather than for a specific 2026 presidential matchup.[5][10]

sources.name: New York Times / Embold Research – Salve Regina University Pell Center
sources.details: Embold Research poll for Salve Regina University’s Pell Center of likely Rhode Island Democratic primary voters shows Senator Jack Reed at 61% to Connor Burbridge’s 12%, a Reed +49 Democratic primary margin.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (Democratic primary)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll finds Jack Reed leading Democratic primary challenger Connor Burbridge 53% to 25%, a Reed +28 margin among Democratic voters.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (Democratic primary, earlier wave)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll reports Reed at 65% to Burbridge’s 15% in the Democratic primary, a Reed +50 margin.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (general-election hypothetical vs. McKay)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Survey Center general-election test shows Jack Reed leading Republican Raymond McKay 52% to 35%, a Reed +17 margin in a hypothetical 2026 Senate matchup.

sources.name: Salve Regina University Pell Center / Embold Research
sources.details: Salve Regina University Pell Center release summarizes Embold Research polling showing Reed backed by more than six in ten Democratic voters, with 12% support for Connor Burbridge and about one-fifth undecided in the Senate primary.

sources.name: Octagon elections forecast (Rhode Island Senate winner)
sources.details: Octagon’s aggregated forecast, drawing on Cook, DDHQ, Inside Elections, and Sabato, estimates Democratic odds of winning the Rhode Island Senate seat at roughly 98%, describing the race as heavily favoring the Democratic incumbent.

sources.name: PredictionMarketsPicks – Rhode Island Senate 2026 odds
sources.details: Prediction-market odds show the Democratic Party contract for Rhode Island’s 2026 Senate race trading at 97¢, implying about a 97% chance of a Democratic hold.

sources.name: Polymarket – Rhode Island Senate Election Margin of Victory
sources.details: A margin-of-victory prediction market on the Rhode Island Senate race shows the most likely outcome bucket as Democrat winning by 30%+ (priced at 46%), with the next most likely bucket Democrat by 25–30% (15%), reinforcing expectations of a very large Democratic margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Statewide PVI (via summary table)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index lists Rhode Island’s statewide partisan lean as D+8 relative to the national popular vote in recent presidential elections.
sources.date_range: Statewide PVI based on recent presidential cycles (as of 2026 updates)
